thread:
incident-bot: INCIDENT: High-severity: multiple GPU host reboots detected in us-central1 affecting inference-pool-3. Paging alice_oncall and infra on-call.
alice_oncall: On it. seeing alerts for increased 5xxs from /v1/generate on customers behind inference-pool-3. Starting triage.
monitoring-bot: Alert detail: 3 hosts in pool lost GPU device and rebooted within 15m. Avg 95th latency spike 900ms -> 2.4s. Error rate to 6% for 10m. Links: https://monitoring.redwood/alerts/ALERT-191234
alice_oncall: Can someone grab the host IDs and kernel logs? I want to know if these were OOMs, host reboots, or GPU reset events.
ben_infra: I see 3 instances: gcs-usc-3-12, gcs-usc-3-19, gcs-usc-3-26. All show PCIe AER errors followed by NVRM GPU watchdogs then host reboot. Pasting dmesg head for gcs-usc-3-19:
```
[ 12345.678901] pcieport 0000:00:1c.0: AER: Uncorrected (Non-Fatal) error received: Detected Uncorrected (Non-Fatal) error
[ 12345.679012] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:05:00): 79, pid=1024, GPU has fallen off the bus.
[ 12345.680000] Kernel panic - not syncing: Attempted to kill init!
```
ben_infra: Also saw ECC correctable counter jumps on Xid 79 occurrences. Nvidia driver reports memory ECC corrected counts spiking before the GPU fell off the bus.
carla_sre: Customer impact? Which tenants routed to those hosts? Any retries/queued work lost?
derek_cs: Customer-visible: acme-ml and speedops reported intermittent 5xx, some streaming sessions cut. CS ticket 7892 opened. Impact window ~ 2026-03-15 18:02 - 18:12 UTC. Customers seeing latency + dropped streams.
eve_mleng: From model-side metrics, we see requests timed out mid-generation; KV-cache was lost for in-flight sessions when pods moved. Quality unaffected but sessions restarted.
alice_oncall: Ok, immediate mitigation steps: (1) cordon nodes in pool to prevent scheduling (2) drain remaining nodes gracefully (3) migrate critical traffic to fallback pool (classic-s1) with capacity.
ben_infra: Doing cordon+drain now: `kubectl cordon gcs-usc-3-* && kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets gcs-usc-3-19`.
monitoring-bot: Auto-run: shifting 20% traffic to fallback pool per auto-fallback policy.
alice_oncall: Good. Ben, can you collect full dmesg, `nvidia-smi -q -d ECC`, and kern logs and upload to the incident storage? Put links here.
ben_infra: Uploaded logs: https://logs.redwood/internal/incidents/1912345678/gcs-usc-3-19-dmesg.txt
ben_infra: nvidia-smi ECC snapshot: https://logs.redwood/internal/incidents/1912345678/gcs-usc-3-19-nvidiasmi.txt
carla_sre: I'm building a timeline. So far: 17:59 UTC first PCIe AER on gcs-usc-3-26; 18:02 gcs-usc-3-19 fell off bus and rebooted; 18:07 gcs-usc-3-12 similar pattern. Confirmed by provider metrics showing reboots at those timestamps.
alice_oncall: Any noisy neighbor signals? I want to know if other tenants on the same host had high PCIe traffic or sustained MPS usage.
eve_mleng: We had a heavy-burst eval job on gcs-usc-3-19 earlier, but that was scheduled on a different node; checking placement logs now.
ben_infra: From provider (GCE) telemetry, device PCIe link errors correlate with host-level PCIe retries on slot 5. No explicit corrective action from provider yet. I'm opening a support case.
ben_infra: Case number: GCE-INC-342198. Sharing support link: https://console.cloudsupport.google.com/cases/GCE-INC-342198
derek_cs: Noting customer comms: telling acme-ml we degraded to fallback and are investigating root cause. CS to follow up with timeline.
carla_sre: Hypothesis tracking: listing possible causes
- Hypothesis A: Hardware PCIe lane/host firmware regression causing transient link flaps -> leads to GPU drop (evidence: AER logs, vendor reports of link errors).
- Hypothesis B: Noisy neighbor causing sustained PCIe traffic / thermal stress -> triggers device driver/firmware to drop GPU (evidence: partial, need neighbor vm/sched info).
- Hypothesis C: GPU ECC memory cells failing / bit flips causing driver panic -> evidence: ECC corrected counters spike prior to Xid 79.
- Hypothesis D: Kernel/drivers mismatch, recent kernel update rolled out to this host pool -> need to check recent updates.
alice_oncall: Good. Ben, can you query cloud placement API for co-tenants on those host machines in the 30m prior to failures?
ben_infra: Doing it now. Output: gcs-usc-3-19 had 2 preemptible instances running high RX/TX DMA on pci slot; one is `batch-eval-77` (internal eval infra), logged heavy PCIe transfer between 17:50-17:58 UTC. Linking metrics: https://metrics.redwood/internal/eval/batch-eval-77/pci-io
eve_mleng: batch-eval-77 was running a large tokenization+warming job; I'll check if that used GPUDirect or NVLink patterns, could create heavy bus traffic.
carla_sre: Request: preserve the node disks, kernel logs, and avoid immediate repro; we want forensic data. Also take a full snapshot of the host so provider can inspect.
ben_infra: Snapshot requested: provider snapshot id SNAP-191234. Also asked for host-level serial logs.
incident-bot: On-call handoff: ben_infra is primary for infra investigation. alice_oncall moving to incident coordination & customer updates.
alice_oncall: Handing infra to Ben. I'll keep CS looped and update status messages. Carla, can you lead timeline and RCA doc after we have more logs?
carla_sre: Affirmative. I'll start a doc and paste timeline + evidence links. Initial RCA doc link: https://docs.redwood/rca/1912345678
ben_infra: Provider update: they see PCIe link errors and recommend checking host firmware/BIOS and PCIe riser stability. They escalated to hardware team.
ben_infra: Also, kernel shows `NVRM: Xid 79` which typically indicates GPU stopped responding. Driver suggests checking ECC and running `nvidia-bug-report.sh` if it recurs.
derek_cs: CS note: customers advised of degraded service and fallback migration. No SLA breach yet but we're tracking.
alice_oncall: For mitigation: keep pool cordoned until provider confirms hardware health. Spin up replacement hosts from a different zone to restore capacity.
eve_mleng: We'll add a gating rule to avoid scheduling large eval jobs to inference pools; create a placement policy to segregate noisy-batch workloads.
ben_infra: We've implemented real-time node-level PCIe error rate alerting and a temporary autoscaler policy to avoid cyclic rebalances while provider investigates.
carla_sre: Next actions list:
- Collect full GPU driver debug (`nvidia-bug-report.sh`) from affected hosts if reproduced.
- Cross-check kernel/driver versions across pool; roll back recent driver if matched across failed hosts.
- Provider to inspect for riser/slot issues.
- Forensics: preserve snapshots and serial logs.
- Customer follow-up: Derek to provide timeline + root-cause follow-up once confirmed.
alice_oncall: Any urgent asks before I close this on-call thread? If not, moving to post-incident channel once escalated.
ben_infra: Please keep thread open until provider confirms HW replacement or clears nodes. I'll update every 30m or on new evidence.
carla_sre: I'll add hypothesis A/B/C/D acceptance/rejection notes as we get more logs. Currently A and C have strongest signals (A: link flaps; C: ECC spikes). B cannot be ruled out until placement verification complete.
derek_cs: I'll send a short incident blurb to customers: cause = host GPU instability; mitigation = migration to fallback; RCA pending.
alice_oncall: Thanks all. tagging: @ben_infra @carla_sre @derek_cs — keep this thread active for updates. :heavy_check_mark:
monitoring-bot: Incident status: mitigation in progress. Severity: High -> degraded. Next update ETA 30m.
